fixes.explanation: Not that one, friend. Jesus says, "I do not have a demon, but I honor My Father…" He doesn't avoid the Father at all. He says the crowd is the one who dishonors Him.
Yes, stones. "…they picked up stones to throw at Him." It's a heavy ending to the argument, and I think it's worth slowing down for. It comes right after Jesus says, "…before Abraham was born, I am!"
Close in feel, baker, but not what the verse says. It says, "…they picked up stones to throw at Him." Stones, not dust. That's their response to what Jesus just said about Abraham.

I see the thinking, but Jesus draws no line like that. He says, "…everyone who sins is a slave to sin." He's speaking to people who said, "We are Abraham's descendants," and He puts them right in that "everyone." It's about sin, not about where you're from.

Bills are something plenty of people carry, friend. But Jesus isn't talking about that kind of owing here. He says, "…everyone who sins is a slave to sin." His point is about sin holding people, not money.
I get why you'd pick it, friend. But Jesus says, "…if the Son sets you free, you will be free indeed." He circles back to the son in His house picture. The one who frees is the Son.

That does come up in other places (Mark 2:16), but not in this passage. Here Jesus says they are trying to kill Him "…because My word has no place within you." That's the reason He gives, and He gives only that one.
Yes, baker. They declare, "Our only Father is God Himself." Earlier they had said, "Abraham is our father." Jesus answers that claim right away.
Moses, the leader God sent to bring Israel out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), is a fair guess for this crowd. But he's not who they name here. They say, "Our only Father is God Himself."
David, Israel's famous king (2 Samuel 5:3), is a good guess. But they don't name him. They say, "Our only Father is God Himself." Before that, they had only named Abraham.

Herod, the king in Judea when Jesus was born (Matthew 2:1), is a fair guess. But Jesus names someone else. He says, "You belong to your father, the devil…" He's the murderer from the beginning and the father of lies.
Pharaoh, the king of Egypt who oppressed Israel (Exodus 1:8–11), is a fair guess. But Jesus names someone else. He says, "You belong to your father, the devil…" the father of lies.
Careful, baker. Jesus says, "But because I speak the truth, you do not believe Me!" So the statement is true. That's the reason He gives.
It's a natural guess, but Jesus never says that. He says, "The reason you do not hear is that you do not belong to God." That's the reason He gives.

Yes. They ask, "Are we not right to say that You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?" Samaritan is the first thing they call Him, and the demon comes second. Jesus answers the demon part right away.
I see the guess, baker, but that's not what they say here. Their words are, "…You are a Samaritan and You have a demon?" Neither Galilean nor training comes up in their question.
Yes. They ask, "Are You greater than our father Abraham?" They point out that Abraham died, and so did the prophets. Then they ask, "Who do You claim to be?"
Not richer, friend. They ask, "Are You greater than our father Abraham?" Nobody brings up money here. It's about greatness, not wealth.
Yes. Jesus says, "If I said I did not know Him, I would be a liar like you." Then He adds, "But I do know Him, and I keep His word." He says it plainly.
Not torches, friend. The verse says, "…they picked up stones to throw at Him." It's stones. Torches aren't in the verse.
That's what the verse says. "…Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area." John doesn't say how He was hidden, so I won't guess either. The text gives only that He was hidden and went out.
That would be a movie scene, friend. But the verse says, "…Jesus was hidden and went out of the temple area." No rooftops mentioned.
